title: Onboard and Troubleshoot AWS VPC Flow Logs
objectives: Onboard and Troubleshoot AWS VPC Flow Logs
Verify real recorded events, retained failures and current operational evidence.

tasks.instruction: Open Interview workbench → Recorded integration operations → AWS SQS / S3. The fixture retains an actual s3:GetObject denial, three pending fictional SQS notifications and two explicit CloudWatchLogs object versions. Inspect active native aws_sqs_based_s3 inputs.conf and the IAM policy source. No AWS account, connection or real secret is used.

Preserve the SQS receive/delete statement and add an Allow statement for s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::sandbox-v7-vpcflow/*. The bounded policy supports native Version=2012-10-17, Statement, Sid, Effect, Action and Resource, with explicit Deny precedence. Stage the policy and poll once. Expect three recorded events, all notifications acknowledged and the repeated object version recognized as a duplicate. Poll again to verify no duplicate events.

Search index=cloud_logs | stats count, then index=cloud_logs action=REJECT | stats count by dstport and open Job Inspector. Confirm three total flows, two REJECT flows, and actual extracted srcaddr/dstaddr/port/action fields. This adapter decodes plain explicit CloudWatch logEvents JSON; compression and full AWS IAM evaluation are outside scope.

hints: Inspect running source and actual receipts before changing configuration.
Use the paused fixture clock deliberately; verify results through a separate view or query.
